claims.statement: The app-lynx API client selects a transport per request via isNativeMode(), which probes NativeModules through getNativeModules() using a bare-global-or-globalThis lookup and reports native mode only when a real Pictelio* module is present (PictelioApi / PictelioAuth / PictelioSecureStorage / PictelioApp): native mode forwards method, relative path and body to NativeModules.PictelioApi.request into Java PixivApiCore, while web mode uses fetch through the /pixiv-api and /pixiv-oauth dev proxy paths.

In native mode the access_token is held only in the Java heap as the volatile static field PixivApiCore.accessToken and is never returned to JavaScript; PictelioApi.request receives only method/path/body and PixivApiCore.executeRequest injects Authorization, Referer, User-Agent, and optional Accept-Language headers, while PictelioAuth.loginWithRefreshToken returns user info and a rotated refresh token but not the access_token.

PixivApiCore.executeRequest silently handles 401 on the native path by taking a synchronized block that refreshes once (guarded by isRefreshing and an access_token reference-identity check so concurrent 401s share one refresh), then replays the original request with isRetry=true; refreshAccessTokenCore returns null on failure so the original 401 surfaces to JS.

The JS side implements the ADR-0004 401 retry pattern in execWithAuthRetry: a module-level refreshPromise is shared so concurrent UNAUTHORIZED responses await a single onUnauthorizedHandler invocation and then replay their request once, with authStore registering that handler to run performRefresh and report a session error only when a refresh failure also leaves the session not ready.

client.ts enforces a token barrier: authPermanentFailure short-circuits execute/executeRaw with a synchronous throw, and GET requests without a JS access_token await awaitAuthReady() (the authStore-registered restoreToken provider, capped at 10 seconds) before web mode throws UNAUTHORIZED; the gate also covers the native branch because the Java-heap token is produced asynchronously by the OAuth exchange, while POST requests are intentionally not gated.

The app-lynx client supports only the OAuth refresh_token grant: auth.ts's single oauthTokenRequest helper builds the SparkMD5 X-Client-Time/X-Client-Hash signature and client credentials, and native mode delegates to PictelioAuth.loginWithRefreshToken → PixivApiCore.oauthTokenExchange, which writes the access_token into the Java heap; there is no PKCE flow in this client (login is by pasted refresh token).

refresh_token persistence goes through utils/tokenStorage.ts as a dual-path wrapper (IndexedDB in the web-core worker, NativeModules.PictelioSecureStorage Keystore on native), with unquoteNativeString correcting Lynx's JSON-quoted callback strings; authStore.restoreToken dedups concurrent restores via _restoreInFlight, and every login/refresh plus any Java-side rotated token is written back through saveRefreshToken without blocking in-memory state on persistence failure.

429 rate-limit backoff (ADR-0199) wraps execute/executeRaw inside the outer 401 retry: runWithRateLimitBackoff retries only ApiErrorType.RATE_LIMIT using capped exponential backoff with full jitter (default baseDelay 1000ms, maxDelay 30000ms, maxRetries 3), is abortable during the wait, attaches params.attempts on exhaustion, and its config is injected via setRateLimitBackoffConfig so the client does not depend on Pinia.

queryKeys.ts defines as-const factories under a ['pictelio', <resource>, ...] namespace with sub-namespaces for illusts/novels/users/search/watchlist/notifications/settings, enabling prefix invalidation, and queryClient.ts exports a per-cycle singleton defaulting to staleTime 0, retry false, gcTime 30s, refetchOnWindowFocus false, refetchOnReconnect true, and keepPreviousData, with per-query gcTime overrides for stable detail content versus volatile feeds.

classifyError is the single error-normalization point for get/post/requestRaw, mapping proxy_error, fetch TypeErrors, 401/403/429/5xx and unknown statuses to ApiErrorType values, and isOAuthTokenErrorResponse recognizes Pixiv's 400 invalid_grant string and object forms as UNAUTHORIZED so expired/revoked refresh tokens enter the permanent-failure cleanup path.

rewriteUrl normalizes paths in both modes (stripping the Pixiv host from absolute next_url values in native mode, mapping Pixiv hosts to /pixiv-api and /pixiv-oauth proxy paths in web mode), and shouldAttachAuth plus isTrustedPixivHost restrict the bearer header to local proxy paths or exact trusted Pixiv hostnames, rejecting pseudo-suffix domains to prevent access_token leakage.

The JS 401 path in execWithAuthRetry is retry-once rather than a refresh loop: concurrent UNAUTHORIZED failures in one burst share a single module-level refreshPromise created from onUnauthorizedHandler().finally(...), each catcher then replays the wrapped call exactly once so a second UNAUTHORIZED is surfaced to the caller instead of triggering another refresh, and the promise is cleared as soon as the handler settles so a later burst starts a fresh refresh — i.e. one Pixiv refresh-token exchange per burst, which matters because Pixiv rotates single-use refresh tokens.

client.ts deduplicates GET requests by a GET:<path>:<JSON params> key in inflightGetRequests, so identical concurrent reads share one transport execution and therefore one 429 backoff sequence and one 401 single-flight refresh; calls carrying an AbortSignal never join the map (a shared promise would let one caller's abort cancel the others), requestRaw is excluded from dedup so a raw text body is never shared across callers, and the map is cleaned up through a two-callback then because a single finally would derive an unhandled rejection.

A native transport failure reaches JS as PictelioApi.request's cb(0, errMsg, "") and is classified as ApiErrorType.UNKNOWN rather than NETWORK, because the JS branch calls classifyError(status, null, parsed) — the error string never arrives as the error argument and NETWORK maps only from a web fetch TypeError; the explicit native NETWORK error is thrown when isNativeMode() is true but getNativeModules().PictelioApi is absent, with the message 原生 API 模块不可用.

Every per-entity endpoint module is a thin wrapper over apiClient rather than a second networking implementation: reads are apiClient.get(path, params, signal), writes are apiClient.post with a form-encoded object, and server-issued pagination is passed back verbatim as apiClient.get(next_url, undefined, signal) so rewriteUrl and shouldAttachAuth remain the single URL-normalization and bearer-attachment gates; search.ts is the only module adding its own next_url guard (assertPixivUrl accepts only a /pixiv-api path or an exact app-api.pixiv.net hostname, warns and throws otherwise, and is pinned at source level by search.template.test.ts), and the HTML novel body at /webview/v2/novel is the only endpoint using apiClient.requestRaw.

notification.ts exposes exactly two GET endpoints: loadNotifications(nextUrl?) hits GET /v1/notification/list for the first page and then passes the server's next_url through verbatim, while loadNotificationChildren(id, nextUrl?) hits GET /v1/notification/view-more with notification_id required and the older_than cursor carried by next_url; both are plain apiClient.get wrappers returning PixivNotificationListResponse and required no Java change because PictelioApiModule.request forwards an arbitrary path without an endpoint whitelist.

The BYOK LLM translation channel (api/translate.ts plus api/nativeTranslate.ts, backed by the PictelioTranslate native module) is deliberately separate from the Pixiv gateway: it never calls apiClient or PixivApiCore and classifies its failures as TranslationErrorCode instead of ApiErrorType; on the native path the endpoint config and API key live in Keystore/Java (setApiKey, clearEndpoint, probeEndpoint), getEndpoint returns only a redacted mirror with a hasKey flag, and Java assembles the Authorization header for translateStream, the two documented exceptions being the one-shot configuration write that pushes the plaintext key across the bridge and the web-core dev preview where OpenAIResponsesProvider injects Bearer apiKey itself.

Accept-Language is produced per transport: web mode snapshots i18n's locale.value into the request headers at construction time (so in-flight requests keep their language and a switch applies to the next request), while native mode never sends it from JS — PictelioApiModule reads the settings_language pref on its worker thread and resolves everything except "en" to zh-CN through the pure resolveAcceptLanguage, then passes it to PixivApiCore.executeRequest's new nullable overload, which keeps the Lynx bridge signature unchanged under OTA version skew (the retained 5-argument overload delegates with null, i.e. no header).

refresh_token persistence on the native path is implemented by SecureStorageCompat, which reproduces the @aparajita/capacitor-secure-storage layout exactly — AES/GCM/NoPadding with a per-key AndroidKeyStore alias capacitor-storage_<key>, the WSSecureStorageSharedPreferences file, and ciphertext Base64(ciphertext) + U+0010 + Base64(iv) — so already-stored tokens keep decrypting across client version migrations, with tokenStorage.ts selecting this path only when NativeModules.PictelioSecureStorage exists and falling back to IndexedDB in the web-core worker.

oauthTokenRequest is the single OAuth transport helper and is fail-closed: it rejects unless __DEV__ is true and the compile-time __CREDENTIALS__ contain non-empty clientId, clientSecret and hashSecret, because the vue-lynx plugin forces __DEV__ true under dev so the flag alone is not a guard — this prevents an outbound OAuth request from being built without injected credentials.
